body: A few places where the spec quietly drifts from the idea or asks for machinery it never builds. (1) The idea's expected results hinge on 'resistance gene presence' as a predictive feature, and the pipeline dutifully extracts resistance genes via ARIBA — but FR-008 then excludes exactly those genes from every model. So the headline features the research question asks about are thrown away at training time, and what's left (SNP counts per gene, copy numbers) is never shown to carry enough signal. That may be a fine, even admirable, anti-circularity choice, but it changes the question being answered, and the spec doesn't acknowledge the tension. (2) FR-005 demands 'phylogenetically-aware permutation testing... respecting clonal lineages,' yet nowhere in the requirements or data pipeline is there a step to infer a phylogeny or annotate lineages (no tree-building, no MLST/lineage typing). You can't respect clonal structure you never constructed — the null distribution would silently collapse to ordinary label permutation, which is precisely the false-positive machine US-3 says it wants to avoid. (3) FR-003 waves off the split ratios as 'implementation details' and SC-001 defers the success threshold, even though the parent idea specified 70/15/15 and 75% accuracy explicitly — the spec softens concrete commitments into placeholders. (4) The idea's evidence criterion mixes 'AUC-ROC' and 'cross-validated accuracy exceeds 75%'; the spec carries only AUC-ROC forward, so the stated success bar is no longer the one that was promised.
